metadata.title: Detectron2: graph-guided rewrite and validation
metadata.method: A pinned Graphify capability graph and source-free semantic packages guided fresh authors. Independent verifiers retained original tests, checked CPU and GPU observations separately, and ran installed-wheel and fixed-original-state model checks.
metadata.outcome: 89 functional capabilities remain selected, with no authorized exclusions. Selection does not establish that all capabilities are implemented. Material implementation gaps remain; native harness execution readiness is blocked by incomplete coverage. This report presents an independent audit, not a native verification-success record. 1 supplied fixed-state model inference observations failed or errored; their individual outcomes are displayed without changing upstream-test rates.
limitations: All-source functionality preservation is not established; known missing behavior remains explicit even where mapped tests pass.
CPU and GPU rates count test-case/environment pairs separately; unique upstream tests and execution coverage are reported independently.
A smaller production-source count is a size observation, not evidence of retained functionality. Declarative configuration resources are measured separately.
Fixed-state model observations each use one CPU input and do not establish full checkpoint, training or numerical equivalence.

configuration_volume.method: The same path classifier counts configuration directories named configs or _data and YAML/JSON resources in runtime package roots. Root mapping files, reports, test fixtures, datasets used by tests and declared runtime output are excluded. Production source plus disjoint non-source declarative resources totals 76117 original physical lines and 44504 candidate physical lines.
configuration_volume.limitations: Some original Python configuration and category data are represented as candidate JSON. Resource totals can overlap production source and are not additive; only the explicitly non-source resource subtotal is disjoint. This path-based accounting cannot isolate all data literals embedded in arbitrary Python modules, and byte or line reductions do not establish preserved behavior.

methodology: Counts are test-case/environment pairs; distinct_upstream_tests counts each upstream test identifier once across environments.
Selected capabilities and associated checks do not establish that all selected functionality is implemented. Functional steps inherit capability observations and are not independently tested.
Pass rate = passed / (passed + failed or error), restricted to tests that passed on the original.
Execution coverage = conclusive candidate results / tests that passed on the original.
Skipped, blocked, missing and timed-out comparisons are unverified, never passed.
A successful check covers only its recorded inputs and environment, not full semantic equivalence.
Fixed-original-state model comparisons are separate observations and do not enter the upstream-test counts or rates.
Test cases and shared code may map to multiple capabilities; node totals are not additive.
A red node means an associated check failed, not that the fault was localized to that module. Import associations and shared tests are not full feature coverage.
CPU and GPU observations are distinct test-case/environment pairs; a case run in both environments is not two unique upstream tests.

source_and_resource_measurement.method: Production source plus the disjoint non-source declarative resource subtotal. Includes source configuration code once; excludes tests, documentation and binary datasets/assets.
